blocked_reason: A disposable concurrency probe mistakenly passed --fix to tests/fixtures/lint/native-lint.tsrx instead of a temporary copy, changing `var legacy` to `const legacy` during a read-only Scout task. The timing investigation itself reached a decision, but the scope violation requires a bounded Worker restoration before the board can treat the repository as healthy.
summary: Disproved a rule-specific 0.4-second OXC latency. Ten fresh processes for no-debugger, no-var, no-unused-vars, and no-debugger+no-unused-vars on direct TSX and projected TSRX all measured roughly 1.8-2.1 ms median wall time. OXC metadata attributed about 0.02-0.03 ms to parse, 0.013-0.016 ms to semantic construction, and 0.34-0.38 ms to rule configuration plus execution. Five concurrent three-command batches also finished in roughly 2.2-3.7 ms per child. The earlier 0.38-0.47 second observation was a one-off Node test-runner/binary page-in effect; rerunning the same named test measured 4.8-5.0 ms callback time, while --test-isolation=none reduced total Node harness time from 33.5 ms to 9.0 ms without changing the native child. Current OXC hot-path performance is not the cause. P05 should nevertheless retain the real two-rule combination so this remains proven.
rationale: The same binary, source, and rules are consistently sub-3-ms in fresh sequential and concurrent processes, and OXC's internal timing is sub-millisecond. No repeatable rule-specific product cost exists to optimize. The benchmark should still change from no-debugger-only P05 to the two-rule black-box combination used by the correctness contract, without altering thresholds.

worker_package.objective: Restore the retained var fixture and qualify the two-rule combination in P05 without weakening thresholds.
